intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street foods like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided food walk helps uncover hidden gems and local culinary traditions.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small islet, snorkel in the warm waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by local bus or rental car.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local Cretan home or taverna and learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and homemade baklava. Includes a visit to a local market to source fresh ingredients and a full sit-down meal with local wine or raki at the end.

experiences.name: Sunset Taverna Dinner in Oia
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset from the cliffside village of Oia, then dine at a traditional taverna offering fresh grilled octopus, fava dip, tomatokeftedes (tomato fritters), and local Assyrtiko white wine. This quintessential Greek island dining experience combines stunning scenery with authentic Cycladic cuisine.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities – flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange budget airport transfer (shared shuttle or public bus where available). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort Beachfront. Take a short walk to the beach promenade to breathe in the sea air and get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night souvlaki wrap or gyros from a nearby kiosk or 24-hour street food stand near the resort (budget approx. €3–5)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – you arrive late. Have some euros ready for the transfer and a small snack. Confirm resort check-in arrangements in advance as you arrive after 22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a relaxed wake-up, take a slow stroll along the beachfront directly in front of Aegean Bliss Resort. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea for the first time. Explore the immediate resort neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local beach (walking distance from the resort). Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the hot sunny weather. Bring water and sunscreen. Explore the shoreline on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Wander into the nearest village or town center for an evening stroll (volta). Browse local shops and tavernas along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, yogurt with honey, and fruit from a local bakery or mini-market near the resort (budget approx. €3–5)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a mini-market (olives, cheese, bread, bottled water) and enjoy a picnic on the beach (budget approx. €4–6)
meals.dinner: Find a simple local taverna in the village. Order grilled sardines or a Greek salad with bread. Ask for the daily special (mageirefta) which is always the cheapest option (budget approx. €8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a reusable water bottle and a small cooler bag from a local shop – essential for beach days on a budget. Sunscreen is expensive in tourist shops; buy it at a supermarket.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and visit the local open-air laiki agora (farmers' market) if one is held nearby – typically on specific weekday mornings. Sample fresh fruits, olives, and local cheeses. This is a great way to experience authentic Greek daily life and stock up on cheap, fresh food.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a quieter, less-touristy beach nearby – ask locals or resort staff for a tip on a hidden cove or less-crowded spot reachable by foot or cheap local bus. Swim and snorkel if you have gear.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to freshen up, then head out for an evening ouzo or local beer at a waterfront kafeneion (traditional Greek café). Watch the sunset over the sea.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita (cheese pie) or spanakopita from a local bakery – a classic cheap Greek breakfast (budget approx. €2–3)
meals.lunch: Fresh produce from the morning market – tomatoes, cucumbers, olives, feta, bread (budget approx. €4–5)
meals.dinner: Souvlaki plate at a local grill house – pork or chicken skewers with pita, tzatziki, and salad. One of the best budget meals in Greece (budget approx. €7–10)

day_by_day.notes: Ouzo is traditionally served with a small free meze (snack) in many traditional kafeneions – great value. A small carafe of house wine at tavernas is usually very affordable (€4–6).

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or cheap shared taxi to a nearby archaeological site or ancient ruins in the region. Explore the history at your own pace. Many smaller sites in Greece have free or very low-cost entry (€2–6).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ruins, find a shaded café in the nearest town for a cold Greek frappe or freddo espresso. Browse the town's backstreets and local shops. Visit a small Byzantine church if one is nearby – free entry and beautifully atmospheric.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by local bus. Enjoy a swim at the resort beach as the heat of the day fades. The sea is warm well into the evening.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a local café near the resort (budget approx. €3–5)
meals.lunch: Gyros wrap from a street-food stand near the archaeological site or in the nearby town (budget approx. €3–4)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using market produce if your accommodation has kitchen access, or visit a local psistaria (grill restaurant) for grilled meats with sides (budget approx. €8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Always carry a refillable water bottle. Temperatures will be around 29°C so hydration is critical, especially when visiting exposed ancient sites. Wear a hat and light clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach morning at the resort's beachfront. Arrive early to claim a good spot before it gets busy. Swim, float, and relax. Watch for local fishermen bringing in their morning catch – a lovely authentic sight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short local bus ride to a neighboring beach or bay. Greece's coastline offers tremendous variety even within short distances. Explore rock formations, sea caves, or crystal-clear shallow areas perfect for snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local fish taverna for dinner – ask for the catch of the day (psari tis imeras). Eating fresh fish is more affordable at non-tourist-facing local tavernas away from the main waterfront strip.

meals.breakfast: Homemade-style breakfast from a mini-market: fresh bread, tomatoes, feta, olives, and orange juice (budget approx. €4–6)
meals.lunch: Snacks on the beach – pack from a mini-market: crackers, hummus, fruit, and water (budget approx. €4–5)
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish at a local taverna – choose a smaller, less-touristy spot. Pair with a village salad and a glass of local wine (budget approx. €12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Grilled octopus hanging outside a taverna is a sign of authenticity and freshness. Octopus is often very affordable and delicious. Avoid restaurants with laminated picture menus near tourist hotspots – they tend to be overpriced.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip by local ferry or bus to a nearby island or coastal village (depending on your resort's location). Purchase the cheapest ticket available – Greek domestic ferries and regional buses are very affordable. Explore on arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the day-trip destination – swim at a local beach, explore the harbor, and visit a hilltop viewpoint if available. Many small Greek islands and coastal villages have spectacular panoramic views accessible on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by evening ferry or bus. Enjoy a relaxed dinner close to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure – grab a pastry and coffee from a local bakery (budget approx. €3–4)
meals.lunch: At the day-trip destination – look for a simple taverna away from the harbor front. Order a mezedes (shared small plates) spread for the most affordable and authentic experience (budget approx. €8–12)
meals.dinner: Simple meal near the resort – a gyros or souvlaki wrap, or a light Greek salad with bread (budget approx. €5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry or bus schedules in advance and buy return tickets early. Carry cash as smaller destinations may not accept cards. Bring sunscreen, water, and a light bag for the day trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and slow morning at the resort. This is your midpoint rest day. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and take a gentle swim. Reflect on the first half of your trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate area around Aegean Bliss Resort on foot. Look for hidden paths along the coast, local chapels, or viewpoints. Take photographs and enjoy the scenery without rushing.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner to celebrate the midpoint of your trip – still budget-conscious but perhaps a full three-course meal at a good local taverna with a sea view.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a local café – eggs, olives, cheese, tomatoes, bread, and coffee (budget approx. €5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch – a simple Greek salad and a cold beer or lemonade at a beachside café (budget approx. €6–8)
meals.dinner: Three-course taverna meal: start with taramosalata or tzatziki and bread, main of moussaka or pastitsio, finish with a complimentary dessert (many tavernas offer loukoumades or fruit). House carafe of wine included (budget approx. €15–18)

day_by_day.notes: Moussaka and pastitsio are classic Greek oven-baked dishes (mageirefta) that are hearty, delicious, and very affordable. They are often made fresh in the morning and are the best value on the menu.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk along the beach before the crowds arrive. The light in the early morning on the Aegean is spectacular. Collect sea glass or shells. Watch local fishermen at the harbor if one is nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach that requires a short hike to reach – these are almost always less crowded and more beautiful. Ask resort staff for recommendations. Bring plenty of water and snacks for the hike.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local ouzeri or mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) for a traditional Greek evening of shared small plates and ouzo or tsipouro.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri (sesame bread ring) bought from a street vendor or bakery, with a freddo cappuccino (budget approx. €2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic at the hidden beach – pack from a mini-market: pita bread, hummus, cucumber, tomatoes, and cheese (budget approx. €4–6)
meals.dinner: Mezedes spread at a local ouzeri – order 3–4 small plates to share: grilled octopus, saganaki (fried cheese), gigantes (giant beans), and dolmades (stuffed vine leaves). Ouzo or local wine included (budget approx. €12–16)

day_by_day.notes: At a mezedopoleio, ordering mezedes (small plates) is the most social and often most affordable way to eat. You can control your spending by ordering plates gradually. Ouzo is almost always served with a small complimentary snack.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to the nearest larger town or city in the region. Explore its central market (agora), main square (plateia), and any free or low-cost cultural sites such as a local museum, archaeological collection, or historic waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the town. Visit a local supermarket to stock up on affordable Greek pantry items: honey, olives, olive oil, and local wine or spirits to enjoy back at the resort or take home as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by local bus. Enjoy a quiet evening on the beachfront, perhaps with a bottle of local wine purchased from the supermarket, watching the stars over the sea.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the resort or grab a quick pastry en route (budget approx. €2–4)
meals.lunch: Eat in the town's central market area – look for a ladokolla (greasy spoon) or a bakery selling fresh pies. A slice of spanakopita or a cheese pie is filling and cheap (budget approx. €3–5)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal back at the resort using supermarket ingredients, or pick up a ready-made meal from a local deli or supermarket hot counter (budget approx. €5–8)

day_by_day.notes: Greek supermarkets (AB Vassilopoulos, Sklavenitis, or local chains) have excellent ready-made food sections with affordable hot dishes. Local honey and olive oil make wonderful budget-friendly souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the resort beach. Try renting a paddleboard or kayak if available at low cost from a local rental stand – a fun way to explore the coastline from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby traditional Greek village inland if accessible by local bus. Explore its stone-paved streets, central kafeneion, and small church. Chat with locals if you get the chance – Greeks are famously hospitable.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast for a sunset swim. The Aegean at sunset is one of the most beautiful sights in the world. Afterward, enjoy dinner at a waterfront taverna.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt with local honey and fresh fruit from a mini-market (budget approx. €3–5)
meals.lunch: At the inland village kafeneion – order a simple Greek coffee and whatever food they offer: perhaps a homemade pie or a simple salad (budget approx. €4–7)
meals.dinner: Grilled lamb chops (paidakia) or chicken at a local taverna – one of the most iconic Greek grill dishes, often very affordable at non-tourist spots. Served with fries and salad (budget approx. €10–14)

day_by_day.notes: Paddleboard and kayak rentals are usually €8–15 per hour. Sharing with a travel companion cuts costs in half. Inland villages are often completely off the tourist trail and offer an authentic glimpse into traditional Greek life.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning snorkeling session directly from the resort beach or a nearby rocky cove. The warm, clear Aegean water in June is perfect for underwater exploration. Bring or rent a basic mask and snorkel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and read on the beach. This is your dedicated lazy afternoon. Enjoy the sun responsibly – take a break in the shade during peak heat (13:00–16:00). Build sandcastles, swim, or simply float in the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Take a long evening walk along the beachfront promenade. Stop for a cold drink at a beach bar. Watch the fishing boats return to harbor as the sun goes down.

meals.breakfast: Fresh-squeezed orange juice and a cheese or spinach pie from a local bakery (budget approx. €3–5)
meals.lunch: Beach snack plate – olives, feta, cherry tomatoes, bread, and a cold Mythos or Alfa beer from a beach kiosk (budget approx. €6–8)
meals.dinner: Try a local psarotaverna (fish taverna) for grilled calamari or shrimp saganaki with a village salad and house wine (budget approx. €12–15)

day_by_day.notes: Snorkel gear rental is typically €5–8 for a half day. If you plan multiple snorkeling days, buying a basic set from a local shop (€10–15) may be more economical. The Aegean has excellent visibility in June.

day_by_day.morning: Final full exploration day. Revisit your favorite beach or spot from the trip. Take photos, collect memories, and enjoy the warm Aegean one more time. Consider writing a travel journal entry or postcard to send home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at local shops – avoid tourist traps near main squares. Look for local products: olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, local spirits (tsipouro or mastiha liqueur), and handmade ceramics. These are the best-value authentic Greek souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite taverna from the trip, or try somewhere new that you spotted earlier in the holiday. Celebrate a wonderful 13 days in Greece.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek café breakfast to mark the final full day – coffee, eggs, bread, cheese, olives, and tomatoes (budget approx. €5–8)
meals.lunch: Light lunch – a simple gyros wrap or a fresh salad at a beachside café (budget approx. €5–7)
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner – order a spread: starter mezedes, a main dish each, dessert of baklava or galaktoboureko (custard pastry), and a carafe of local wine. Splurge slightly on this final night (budget approx. €18–22)

day_by_day.notes: Baklava and galaktoboureko from a local zacharoplasteio (patisserie) are excellent and very affordable Greek desserts (€1.50–3 per piece). Many tavernas also offer complimentary dessert or a small carafe of local spirit at the end of a meal – a wonderful Greek tradition called kerasma.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise swim in the Aegean. Pack your bags and complete checkout formalities at Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with reception if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a local café. Take a last slow walk along the beachfront. Arrange your airport transfer – book a shared shuttle or use public transport to keep costs down.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, local food, and Greek sunshine.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast – a koulouri with coffee, or a full café breakfast if time allows (budget approx. €3–6)
meals.lunch: Light airport meal or a final gyros wrap from a street stand near the resort before departing (budget approx. €4–7)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Keep some euros aside for airport transfers, departure taxes, and last-minute airport snacks. Greek airports have reasonable café options airside. Double-check your flight details and terminal the night before. Kalo taxidi – have a great journey!

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room. Take a short stroll on the resort terrace to enjoy the warm night air and sea breeze.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the resort bar or a quick bite from a nearby 24-hour souvlaki stand upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — priority is rest after a long flight. Confirm your room is ready, request an early breakfast if needed, and plan for a full Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. After breakfast, take your first walk along the resort's beachfront. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea and get your bearings around the local area. Pick up a local map and chat with the concierge about nearby highlights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest local beach town for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing. Rent a sunbed and umbrella (approx. €8–12) and enjoy the crystal-clear water. Explore the beach promenade, browse small souvenir shops, and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village for your first proper Greek dinner. Find a family-run taverna with outdoor seating and order classic dishes to share.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — enjoy fresh fruit, Greek yogurt with honey, and pastries
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar — grilled corn, fresh-squeezed orange juice, or a cheese pie (tyropita)
meals.dinner: Local taverna — order a Greek salad, tzatziki, grilled octopus, and fresh bread. Budget €20–30 per person with a carafe of local wine

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — your body is still adjusting to the time zone. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen generously; the Greek sun is strong even in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a morning swim before the beaches get crowded — the sea is warm and calm in the early hours. After your swim, visit the local morning market (laiki agora) if one is running nearby. Browse fresh produce, olives, local cheeses, and herbs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day guided boat trip or rent a small pedal boat to explore sea caves and hidden coves along the coastline. Many local operators offer affordable tours (€25–45 per person). Snorkeling gear is often included.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort to rinse off and relax. Head out for dinner at a seaside restaurant where you can watch the sunset over the water.

meals.breakfast: Grab a sesame koulouri (bread ring) and a Greek coffee from a local bakery near the market
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the morning market — olives, cheese, fruit — to enjoy on the boat, or stop at a harbor-side cafe for a light meal
meals.dinner: Seaside restaurant — try fresh grilled fish of the day, horta (wild greens), and a cold Mythos beer. Budget €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip the evening before or first thing in the morning as spots fill up quickly in June. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and water shoes for the sea caves.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning hike or scenic walk along a coastal path near the resort. Many Greek coastal areas have well-marked trails with stunning clifftop views over the Aegean. Start early before the heat peaks — depart by 8:00 AM and aim to be back by 10:30 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at a quieter, less-touristy beach discovered during your explorations. Bring a book, snorkel, or simply float in the sea. The water temperature in June is around 24–26°C — perfect for extended swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the local village square (plateia) in the early evening for the traditional Greek 'volta' — a leisurely evening stroll. Join locals at a kafeneion (traditional coffee house) for a frappe or ouzo with mezedes.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local bakery — try spanakopita (spinach pie) and a freddo espresso
meals.lunch: Beachside taverna — a simple plate of calamari, village salad, and pita bread with dips. Budget €12–18 per person
meals.dinner: Kafeneion or mezedopoleion — order a spread of small plates: dolmades, saganaki (fried cheese), taramosalata, and grilled halloumi. Budget €18–25 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy sandals or trail shoes for the coastal walk. Carry at least 1 liter of water per person. The afternoon beach is best enjoyed between 15:00–18:00 when the midday heat begins to ease.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby historic site or ancient ruins (check with the concierge for the closest archaeological site — could be a temple, ancient theater, or Byzantine castle). Arrive early when it opens to beat the heat and the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the historic site, explore the nearest town's old quarter. Walk through narrow whitewashed alleyways, visit a small local museum (entry usually €3–6), and browse artisan shops selling ceramics, jewelry, and handmade goods.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and enjoy a swim at the resort beach as the sun lowers. Have dinner at a restaurant specializing in traditional Greek cuisine — look for a spot with a wood-fired oven.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fuel up for a day of sightseeing
meals.lunch: In the old town — find a small psistaria (grill house) for a souvlaki plate with tzatziki and chips. Budget €10–15 per person
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna with wood-fired dishes — try moussaka, slow-roasted lamb, or pastitsio. Budget €22–32 per person with local wine

day_by_day.notes: Bring comfortable walking shoes, a hat, and sunglasses for the historic site. Many sites close or reduce hours on Mondays — check in advance. Carry cash as smaller establishments may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a Greek cooking class or food experience. Many local operators offer 2–3 hour morning classes (€45–70 per person) where you learn to make dishes like spanakopita, tzatziki, and baklava using local ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class (and tasting your creations!), head to the beach for a relaxed afternoon. Try paddleboarding or kayaking — rental equipment is widely available at Greek beach resorts for €10–20 per hour.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sundowner cocktail at a clifftop or rooftop bar if one is available nearby. Watch the famous Greek sunset with a glass of local wine or a Aperol Spritz.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before the cooking class
meals.lunch: Eat what you cooked in the class — this is part of the experience!
meals.dinner: Fish taverna by the water — order whole grilled sea bream or sea bass, priced by weight (€12–18 per kg). Share a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine. Budget €28–38 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 2–3 days in advance. Ask the class instructor for recommendations on where locals actually eat — they always know the best hidden gems.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend the morning lounging by the resort pool or on the beach. Read, journal, or simply do nothing — this is Greece, after all.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle afternoon walk to explore the immediate neighborhood around the resort. Pop into a local mini-market to stock up on Greek snacks — local honey, nuts, dried figs, and olive oil make great gifts or personal treats.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local sunset sailing cruise if available in the area (€35–60 per person for a 2-hour trip). These typically include light snacks, wine, and a chance to swim off the boat at anchor.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast — take your time, try everything on the buffet
meals.lunch: Light and local — a gyros wrap from a street-side gyradiko. Budget €3–5 per wrap
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant for convenience — try the catch of the day or a mezedes platter. Treat yourself to a dessert of loukoumades (honey doughnuts) or galaktoboureko

day_by_day.notes: This is your halfway point — a slower day helps prevent travel fatigue. Use this evening to review the second half of your itinerary and make any bookings needed for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a different beach today — research a beach 20–40 minutes away that has a different character (perhaps a pebbly cove, a lagoon-style bay, or a beach with dramatic rock formations). Take a local bus, taxi, or rent a scooter/ATV for the day (€25–40).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the new beach location. If snorkeling, look for sea urchins, octopus, and colorful fish among the rocks. Many Greek beaches have small beach bars where you can order cold drinks and simple food without leaving the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the resort area and stop in a different village than you've visited before. Find a psarotaverna (fish taverna) for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack a breakfast to go — yogurt, fruit, and a pastry from a local bakery to eat on the way
meals.lunch: Beach bar at the new beach — grilled sardines, a salad, and cold Alfa beer. Budget €15–20 per person
meals.dinner: Psarotaverna — grilled prawns, mussel saganaki, and fresh catch. Budget €25–35 per person with a carafe of house white wine

day_by_day.notes: If renting a scooter or ATV, ensure you have an appropriate license and always wear a helmet. Check the fuel level before heading out. Download an offline map in case mobile signal is patchy on rural roads.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local olive grove or winery for a morning tour and tasting. Greece has a rich tradition of olive oil and wine production — many small producers offer informal tours and tastings for €10–20 per person. This is a wonderful insight into Greek agricultural life.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tasting, stop by a local monastery or hilltop chapel if one is nearby. These are often free to enter, beautifully maintained, and offer panoramic views. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered).
day_by_day.evening: Back at the resort, enjoy a final swim of the day as the sun sets. Then head out for dinner at a restaurant you've been meaning to revisit, or try somewhere new based on recommendations gathered during the trip.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local cafe — try a bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) if you haven't yet
meals.lunch: At or near the olive grove/winery — many offer a simple meze spread with their products. Budget €12–18 per person
meals.dinner: Recommended local taverna — order slow-cooked stifado (beef stew with onions and spices) or lamb kleftiko. Budget €22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Call ahead or have the hotel arrange the olive grove or winery visit — many small producers appreciate advance notice. Buy a bottle of local olive oil or wine to take home as a souvenir.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day excursion to a nearby island if accessible by ferry (many Greek coastal resorts are close to day-trip islands). Ferries typically depart 08:00–09:00 and return by 17:00–18:00. Buy tickets the day before (€15–30 round trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the day-trip island — walk through the main town, visit the harbor, swim at a local beach, and browse the shops. Island towns are often beautifully preserved with Cycladic or Venetian architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to the mainland and make your way back to the resort. Have a relaxed dinner near the harbor or at the resort after a full day of travel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the ferry departure
meals.lunch: On the island — find a harbor-front taverna for grilled fish, a Greek salad, and fresh bread. Budget €18–25 per person
meals.dinner: Easy and relaxed — resort restaurant or a nearby casual eatery. Try a simple pasta with seafood or a pizza from a local wood-fired spot. Budget €15–22 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check the ferry schedule carefully and note the last return time. Wear comfortable shoes for walking on the island — cobblestones can be uneven. Bring cash, sunscreen, and a light layer for the ferry ride.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the resort beach for a final extended swim and snorkel session. The sea is at its warmest in late June. Take underwater photos if you have a waterproof camera or phone case.
day_by_day.afternoon: Go souvenir and gift shopping in the local town. Look for authentic Greek products: hand-painted ceramics, evil eye (mati) charms, local honey, saffron from Kozani, mastiha products, and natural sea sponges.
day_by_day.evening: Book a special dinner at one of the better restaurants in the area for a celebratory pre-departure meal. Dress up slightly and enjoy a longer, more indulgent dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — your last few mornings, make the most of it
meals.lunch: Street food in town — a souvlaki wrap and fresh lemonade while shopping. Budget €5–8 per person
meals.dinner: Upscale taverna or seafood restaurant — splurge slightly on a special meal. Try lobster pasta (astakomakaronada), grilled whole fish, and a bottle of Assyrtiko. Budget €40–55 per person

day_by_day.notes: When shopping for souvenirs, avoid mass-produced items sold at tourist hotspots. Look for shops run by local artisans — the quality and authenticity are far superior and your money supports local families.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise walk along the beach — a magical and quiet moment before the day begins. Take photos, collect a small shell or pebble as a memento, and reflect on the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at leisure — a final swim, reading by the pool, or a gentle walk through areas you haven't fully explored. Visit any spots on your list that you haven't yet ticked off.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner with a view. Find a restaurant with the best sunset view you can — a clifftop spot, a rooftop terrace, or a beachfront table. Order your favorite dishes from the trip and toast to Greece.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast — Greek yogurt, honey, walnuts, and fresh fruit
meals.lunch: Casual beachside meal — mezedes spread, cold beer, and fresh bread. Budget €15–20 per person
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a scenic restaurant — revisit your favorite dish or try something you haven't yet. Order baklava or loukoumades for dessert. Budget €30–40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing this evening to avoid a stressful final morning. Confirm your checkout time with the resort and arrange airport transfer if needed. Keep one outfit and toiletries accessible for the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece. Enjoy one last breakfast at the resort. Take a short final walk on the beach or sit on the balcony with a Greek coffee. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, you may have time at the airport to browse duty-free for last-minute Greek products — mastiha liqueur, olive oil, and Greek sweets like pasteli (sesame honey bars) travel well.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with a full heart, a tan, and wonderful memories of beaches, food, and the warm Greek hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — enjoy it slowly
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or cafe — pick up a final Greek snack or meal before your flight
meals.dinner: On the plane or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and boarding at Greek airports, which can be busy in summer. Keep your travel documents, valuables, and any fragile souvenirs in your carry-on bag.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, dramatic limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street foods like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided food walk helps uncover hidden gems and local culinary traditions.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small islet, snorkel in the warm waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by local bus or rental car.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink at the resort's night bar, and enjoy a light late-night snack from room service.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night room service: charcuterie board, local olives, fresh bread, and a glass of Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the resort's concierge. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a private guided orientation tour of the immediate coastal area. Explore the resort's beachfront, take a refreshing morning swim in the warm Aegean Sea, and settle into the luxury surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a half-day private boat charter along the local coastline. Discover hidden coves, snorkel in crystal-clear waters, and soak up the hot June sunshine. The captain can guide you to secluded swimming spots inaccessible by land.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's clifftop or beachfront bar, followed by a fine dining dinner at the resort's signature restaurant featuring contemporary Greek cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the resort restaurant: fresh pastries, local honey, yogurt with figs, eggs, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Onboard the boat charter: a curated mezze picnic with grilled octopus, tzatziki, spanakopita, fresh fruit, and chilled local rosé
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant: grilled sea bream with lemon-caper butter, slow-roasted lamb chops, and a bottle of Domaine Sigalas Santorini red

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter through the resort concierge the evening of arrival. Sunscreen and a hat are essential — temperatures will reach 29°C.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — take a luxury private transfer into Athens and join an exclusive guided food tour of the Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market). Explore stalls overflowing with spices, fresh fish, cured meats, and regional cheeses. Meet local vendors and learn the stories behind Greece's most beloved ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Athens food experience with a private cooking class in a boutique Athenian kitchen. Learn to prepare classic Greek dishes using the morning's market finds — moussaka, dolmades, and galaktoboureko for dessert.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Athens' top fine dining restaurants in Kolonaki or Monastiraki neighborhood, then a private transfer back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the resort before departing: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey, walnuts, and seasonal berries
meals.lunch: During the food tour — tastings of fresh produce, artisan cheeses, cured meats, olives, and street food including souvlaki and loukoumades (honey-dipped doughnuts)
meals.dinner: Varoulko Seaside or Hytra Athens (Michelin-recognized): tasting menu featuring modern Greek cuisine — sea urchin with cream, Aegean lobster pasta, and pistachio baklava

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Central Market Food Tour is one of the available curated experiences. Pre-book the private cooking class and dinner reservation well in advance. Round-trip private transfer from the resort to Athens is approximately 30–45 minutes depending on resort location.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the resort early for a private luxury transfer to the port or airport for a short flight or high-speed ferry to Zakynthos (Zante). Check into a premium suite at a luxury clifftop hotel on Zakynthos with panoramic Ionian Sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Boat Tour — take a private or small-group luxury boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed and dramatic beaches. Swim in the electric-blue waters, explore the famous shipwreck, and enjoy the towering white limestone cliffs. Extend the tour to include the Blue Caves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) for a stroll along the Venetian harbor. Enjoy sunset drinks at a waterfront bar before dinner at a top local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before transfer: continental spread with pastries, cold cuts, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Onboard the Navagio boat tour: fresh seafood mezze, grilled prawns, local bread, and chilled white wine enjoyed on deck
meals.dinner: Malanos Restaurant, Zakynthos — a beloved institution serving traditional Zakynthian cuisine: rabbit stifado, fresh fish of the day, and local Verdea wine

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is one of the curated available experiences. Book a private boat charter for the most premium experience — avoid crowded public tours. Arrive at Navagio early afternoon when the light on the cliffs is most spectacular. Wear water shoes as the beach is pebbled.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the interior of Zakynthos with a private guided jeep tour through the island's lush green hills and traditional villages. Visit Keri village and the dramatic Keri Cliffs, and stop at a family-run olive oil estate for a private tasting and tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the coast for a relaxed afternoon at Gerakas Beach, one of Zakynthos' most beautiful and protected beaches (a sea turtle nesting site). Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the calm turquoise waters.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset sailing cruise around the southern tip of Zakynthos with champagne service on deck. Return to the hotel for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast: full spread including local Zakynthian specialties — mandolato nougat, pasteli sesame bars, fresh figs, and eggs
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the hotel: cold cuts, local cheeses, olives, stuffed vine leaves, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Zakynthos hotel restaurant or Prosilio Restaurant: fresh catch of the day baked in rock salt, grilled vegetables with local olive oil, and loukoumades with honey and cinnamon

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has restrictions during turtle nesting season (June–August) — no umbrellas allowed in certain zones and beach closes at dusk. Respect the conservation rules. The olive oil tasting is a highlight not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Fly or take a ferry from Zakynthos to Crete (Heraklion or Chania). Private luxury transfer to a premium beachfront resort or boutique hotel in the Chania region of western Crete.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, explore the enchanting old Venetian harbor of Chania on foot. Walk through the narrow cobblestone streets of the old town, browse artisan shops, and admire the historic lighthouse and Venetian fortifications.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Chania's harbor district at one of Crete's most acclaimed restaurants, followed by an evening stroll along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Zakynthos hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Upon arrival in Chania: lunch at Thalassino Ageri — a legendary fish taverna on the seafront serving ultra-fresh Cretan seafood: grilled calamari, sea urchin salad, and fish soup
meals.dinner: Tamam Restaurant, Chania (housed in a former Turkish bathhouse): Cretan-Mediterranean fusion — lamb with stamnagathi greens, dakos salad, and warm chocolate lava cake with Cretan honey ice cream

day_by_day.notes: The transfer between islands can be done via a short domestic flight (most efficient) or an overnight ferry for a more scenic experience. Book flights well in advance as June is peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip — depart early for the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, approximately 75 km from Chania. Arrive early (before 10:00) to secure the best spot before crowds arrive. Marvel at the famous pink-tinged sand created by crushed coral and shells, and wade through the shallow lagoon to the small island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Elafonissi — snorkel in the clear shallow waters, explore the island's wild dunes and natural rock formations, and relax in the stunning scenery. Pack a premium picnic or dine at the beach taverna.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania in the late afternoon. Freshen up at the hotel, then enjoy a private cooking experience or a curated Cretan food and wine tasting at a local estate.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before departure: yogurt, honey, and Cretan paximadi rusks with olive oil and tomato
meals.lunch: Premium packed picnic from the hotel or lunch at Elafonissi Taverna: grilled fish, Greek salad, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Cretan food and wine pairing dinner at a boutique winery near Chania: aged graviera cheese, slow-cooked lamb with herbs, wild greens pie, and Cretan Liatiko red wine

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi Beach is one of the curated available experiences. Arrive before 09:30 to avoid the peak crowds that gather by midday. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. The drive through the White Mountains is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hike through the world-famous Samaria Gorge — one of Europe's longest gorges at 16 km. Walk through dramatic landscapes, towering rock walls, and ancient ruins. The trail ends at the small village of Agia Roumeli on the Libyan Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reward yourself with a swim at Agia Roumeli beach — a remote, wild beach accessible only by foot or boat. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Sougia or Hora Sfakion, then a private transfer back to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the hotel spa — book a traditional Cretan herbal massage or a couple's treatment using local olive oil and herbs. Light dinner at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hearty breakfast before the hike: scrambled eggs, Cretan sausage, whole grain bread, fresh orange juice, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Taverna at Agia Roumeli: simple, satisfying post-hike meal of grilled lamb chops, village salad, and cold Mythos beer or fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the hotel: mezze platter with hummus, taramosalata, grilled halloumi, stuffed peppers, and a glass of chilled Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge hike is strenuous (6–8 hours). Wear proper hiking shoes and carry at least 2 liters of water. The gorge is open May–October. Book the return ferry transfer in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Crete to Santorini (short 45-minute flight). Private luxury transfer to a premium cave suite hotel in Oia or Imerovigli with iconic caldera views. Check in and soak in the extraordinary scenery from your private terrace or infinity pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the village of Oia on foot — wander through the iconic blue-domed churches, browse high-end boutiques and art galleries, and discover quiet alleyways away from the main tourist path. Visit the Oia Castle ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset from Oia Castle — arrive early to claim a premium viewpoint. Follow with dinner at one of Oia's celebrated caldera-view restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Crete hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Upon arrival in Santorini: lunch at Ammoudi Bay (below Oia) — fresh lobster, grilled octopus, and sea urchin at one of the waterfront tavernas (Dimitris or Katina's)
meals.dinner: 1800 Restaurant, Oia — set inside a restored captain's mansion: tasting menu with Santorini tomato fritters, fava puree, Aegean sea bass, and volcanic wine pairings from Santo Wines

day_by_day.notes: June is peak season in Santorini — the Oia sunset viewpoint becomes extremely crowded. Arrive at least 90 minutes before sunset to secure a good spot, or arrange a private sunset sailing cruise for a more exclusive experience. Book dinner reservations months in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private catamaran or luxury sailing cruise around the Santorini caldera. Visit the volcanic hot springs at Palea Kameni, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and explore the whitewashed village of Thirassia — the quieter, less-visited island across the caldera.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the sailing cruise with a stop at Red Beach near Akrotiri — one of the most dramatic beaches in Greece with towering red volcanic cliffs. Swim and explore before returning to the boat for the sail back.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the acclaimed Santo Wines winery perched on the caldera cliff for a premium private tasting of Santorini's volcanic wines — Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto. Paired with local cheeses and bites while watching the sunset over the caldera.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast on your private terrace: fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and Freddo espresso overlooking the caldera
meals.lunch: Onboard the catamaran: BBQ lunch with grilled prawns, fresh fish, Greek salad, and chilled local wine served on deck
meals.dinner: Selene Restaurant, Fira or Pyrgos — Santorini's most prestigious dining institution: modern Cycladic cuisine using hyper-local ingredients — Santorini fava, cherry tomatoes, capers, and fresh catch with volcanic mineral wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter through the hotel concierge for the most exclusive experience. The hot springs water stains swimwear — wear an older swimsuit. Thirassia is a hidden gem and far less crowded than Santorini's main island.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the ancient ruins of Akrotiri — Santorini's remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' A private guided tour brings the 3,600-year-old civilization to life. The site is fully covered and comfortable even in the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on Santorini's black volcanic sand coastline. Relax on premium sun loungers at a beach club, swim in the warm sea, and enjoy the dramatic contrast of the black sand against the turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Helicopter or private transfer to Fira for a final Santorini evening. Cocktails at a rooftop caldera bar, then a farewell dinner in Fira or Imerovigli.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast: traditional Santorinian spread with Chloro fresh cheese, sun-dried tomatoes, capers, honey, and warm bread
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Wet Stories Beach Bar & Restaurant, Perivolos: grilled lobster, sea bass carpaccio, and fresh watermelon juice
meals.dinner: Argo Restaurant, Fira — spectacular caldera views: grilled whole lobster, truffle risotto with local mushrooms, and Vinsanto dessert wine with baklava

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking in peak season. The site is covered and shaded — comfortable even in 29°C heat. Perissa and Perivolos beaches are the best black-sand beach experiences on the island, with premium beach clubs available.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Santorini — a slow, luxurious start. Enjoy a long breakfast on your private terrace or by the infinity pool. Take a final dip in the hotel pool with caldera views. Optional: book a private sunrise yoga session on the terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Fly from Santorini back to Athens (45 minutes). Check into a luxury hotel in Athens (Syntagma or Kolonaki area) for the final night — consider the Hotel Grande Bretagne or the King George Hotel. Afternoon at leisure to explore Athens' upscale neighborhoods.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — explore the illuminated Acropolis on an optional private evening tour, then indulge in a celebratory farewell dinner at Athens' finest restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Extravagant final Santorini breakfast: eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit platter, and a glass of chilled Santorini sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Upon arrival in Athens: rooftop lunch at the Hotel Grande Bretagne's GB Roof Garden with Acropolis views — grilled sea bass, Greek salad, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Spondi Restaurant, Athens (two Michelin stars) — Athens' most celebrated fine dining experience: French-Mediterranean tasting menu with Greek ingredients, paired with an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: The evening Acropolis tour (if available) offers a magical, less-crowded experience of the ancient site illuminated against the night sky. Book the Spondi dinner reservation well in advance — it is one of the hardest tables to secure in Athens.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Depending on departure time, visit the Acropolis Museum — one of the world's finest archaeological museums, located at the foot of the Acropolis. A private guided tour provides an intimate and deeply informative experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for last-minute luxury shopping — Greek jewelry (Lalaounis), olive oil products, local wines, and artisan ceramics make perfect premium souvenirs. Enjoy a final Greek coffee at a chic Kolonaki café.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Athens International Airport for departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 13-day journey through the best of Greece's beaches, cuisine, and ancient culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast: full buffet spread at the Grande Bretagne — pastries, smoked salmon, eggs station, fresh juices, and Greek yogurt with thyme honey
meals.lunch: Final lunch in Kolonaki: Vezene Restaurant — modern Greek cuisine in an elegant setting: grilled lamb cutlets, fava with caramelized onions, and a glass of Naoussa Xinomavro red wine
meals.dinner: Light pre-flight meal at the airport's premium lounge or a final snack at the hotel before transfer

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for the airport transfer and check-in. The Acropolis Museum opens at 08:00 — arrive early on the final morning for a peaceful visit before the crowds. Take home a bottle of Vinsanto dessert wine and premium Greek olive oil as edible souvenirs.
